messages:
jess (Sales): FYI EdgeCorp wants to kick off the Private POC this week. They asked for a quick preflight they can run and return. @sanjay can you own the validation checklist and small runbook we hand them?

sanjay (SE): Yep. Confirming they're going to give us a customer-managed k8s cluster (RKE/Rancher) with GPU node pools, right? Also need kubeconfig and one admin SA for install.

mei (Eng): Correct. Important to be explicit about driver/runtime/cgroup versions. I'll draft the exact commands to run and expected outputs. Keep it short and runnable.

oliver (Infra): Also need network rules + image pull creds. I'll prep a small note about ports and registry access.

jess (Sales): Great. Customer asked whether we need host-level privileges or if they can keep everything namespaced. They prefer least privilege.

sanjay (SE): Install requires scheduling onto GPU nodes and some cluster-level objects (CRDs, RBAC, daemonsets). We can provide a `redwood-installer` manifest that only needs cluster-admin during install; afterwards we can drop privileges. We'll include a script to create a temporary SA with limited TTL.

mei (Eng): Preflight checklist (commands they should run and copy back to us):

```
# 1) GPU driver + CUDA
nvidia-smi
# expected: Driver Version >= 525, CUDA Version >= 11.8 (or shows CUDA compatibility)

# sample output (acceptable):
# +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
# | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 11.8     |
# +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

# 2) Kernel and cgroups
uname -r            # recommended >= 5.15
cat /proc/filesystems | grep cgroup
# cgroup v2 recommended; if cgroup v1, confirm containerd supports it

# 3) Container runtime
crictl info | grep "runtime\|containerd"
# containerd >= 1.6 recommended. runc or crun supported for OCI.

# 4) Kubernetes version
kubectl version --short
# expected Server Version: v1.24 - v1.27 (we support 1.24+; confirm exact tested versions)

# 5) Node GPU capacity and labels
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion} {.status.nodeInfo.containerRuntimeVersion} {.status.capacity.nvidia.com/gpu}{"\n"}{end}'

# 6) NVIDIA device plugin / drivers on k8s
kubectl -n kube-system get ds | grep nvidia
kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin -l app=nvidia-device-plugin --tail=50

# 7) System-level prechecks
# swap off
swapon --show
# time sync
timedatectl status

# 8) Required node labels (we will request these during provisioning)
# Example: add label to GPU nodes
kubectl label node <gpu-node> redwood/inference=enable

# 9) Taints (optional)
# If they want dedicated nodes with NoSchedule
kubectl taint nodes <gpu-node> redwood-dedicated=true:NoSchedule
```

mei (Eng): Minimal software versions we recommend to avoid issues:
- NVIDIA driver >= 525 (older drivers can cause OOM/IPC issues)
- CUDA toolkit 11.8+ for binary compatibility
- nvidia-container-toolkit installed for container runtimes
- containerd 1.6+ (or Docker shim with proper config)
- Kernel >= 5.15, recommended distro kernels (Ubuntu 22.04 / RHEL 8.6+ tested)
- Kubernetes 1.24 - 1.27 (we test on these; newer may work but we should validate)

oliver (Infra): Network / firewall note for their security team to whitelist:
- Outbound from cluster -> Redwood control plane: 443 (HTTPS) and 8443 (management)
- Outbound runtime telemetry -> 9090 (metrics) / 50051 (gRPC) if using managed fallback
- If using NodePort for local testing: 30000-32767 (we prefer LoadBalancer in prod)
- SSH (22) allowed from their admin jump host for debugging

sanjay (SE): Access we need to perform the install (short-lived where possible):
- kubeconfig with cluster-admin or an admin SA kubeconfig (we will provide RBAC manifest to create a temp SA)
- S3/registry pull credentials (or we can provide images if they prefer air-gapped images)
- Optional: KMS info if they want envelopes for secrets (we can integrate customer KMS)

jess (Sales): They also asked about image pulls being blocked by ECR proxy. Can we support a private registry push?

mei (Eng): Yes — two options:
1) Pull from our public registry (requires outbound to registry host and creds)
2) We provide OCI images or tar + Helm chart for offline install (we'll need a short checklist for pulling and loading images into their registry)

# offline: example commands to load images
# ctr -n k8s.io images import images.tar
# or docker load < image.tar

sanjay (SE): For RBAC and least privilege we will ship an installer that creates: CRDs, deployments, daemonsets, and a ClusterRoleBinding for install time. Customers can review and revoke the binding after install. We'll include a one-liner to remove the installer RBAC.

oliver (Infra): I'll prepare a small `edge-poc-network.md` snippet for their network/security teams and an `image-pull-steps.sh` for their infra team. Also will generate a short-lived registry token and pre-signed S3 path for artifacts.

jess (Sales): Perfect. Can you both link the preflight checklist and the artifact instructions in this thread when ready? I want to send a single bundle to EdgeCorp support.

deploy-bot: Installer package v0.9.2 is ready in S3: https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/edge-poc/v0.9.2 (expires in 72h) :package:

mei (Eng): Draft checklist + runbook uploaded to our shared drive, attaching here: https://redwood-internal/drive/edge-poc-preflight (will redact for customers). I'll tidy and post a customer-friendly version in the next message.

sanjay (SE): I'll own the follow-ups with a small validation script they can run and paste outputs here. Plan: run in the afternoon, review outputs, schedule install for tomorrow if green.

jess (Sales): Thanks team — copying customer contact details into outbound. I'll push the bundle after we finalize the wording. :thumbsup:
